q-1071.name: Question 1
q-1071.worked_solution:
For a $2\times 2$ matrix, the determinant is given by the formula

$$
|\begin{aligned}a & b \\ c & d\end{aligned}|=ad-bc.
$$

Using the formula, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}6 & 3 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}| & =6\cdot 1-3\cdot 2 \\  & =6-6 \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

q-317372.worked_solution:

q-317369.name: Question 4
q-317369.worked_solution:
For a $2\times 2$ matrix, the determinant is given by the formula

$$
|\begin{aligned}a & b \\ c & d\end{aligned}|=ad-bc.
$$

Using the formula, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}-\sqrt{3} & 4 \\ \sqrt{3} & 1\end{aligned}| & =-\sqrt{3}\cdot 1-4\cdot \sqrt{3} \\  & =-\sqrt{3}-4\sqrt{3} \\  & =-5\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-127606.name: Question 5
q-127606.problem:
If
$T=[\begin{aligned}v & 2v \\ 2 & v+8\end{aligned}]$
and $det(T)=-4$, what is the value of $v?$
q-127606.worked_solution:
For a $2\times 2$ matrix, the determinant is given by the formula

$$
|\begin{aligned}a & b \\ c & d\end{aligned}|=ad-bc.
$$

Using the formula, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(T) & =|\begin{aligned}v & 2v \\ 2 & v+8\end{aligned}| \\  & =v\cdot (v+8)-2v\cdot 2 \\  & ={v}^{2}+4v\end{aligned}
$$

Since $det(T)=-4$, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(T) & =-4 \\ {v}^{2}+4v & =-4 \\ {v}^{2}+4v+4 & =0 \\ (v+2)^{2} & =0 \\ v & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

q-127606.html:
Question 5
?

If T=[v2v2v+8] and det(T)=−4, what is the value of v?

a
v=−2
b
v=34
c
v=73
d
v=4
e
v=−3
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a 2×2 matrix, the determinant is given by the formula

|abcd|=ad−bc.

Using the formula, we have:

det(T)=|v2v2v+8|=v⋅(v+8)−2v⋅2=v2+4v

Since det(T)=−4, we obtain:

det(T)=−4v2+4v=−4v2+4v+4=0(v+2)2=0v=−2

q-69658.name: Question 6
q-69658.problem:
If
    $U=[\begin{aligned}-v & 5 \\ 4 & 3\end{aligned}]$
and
$\text{det}(U)=4$, what is the value of $v?$
q-69658.worked_solution:
For a $2\times 2$ matrix, the determinant is given by the formula

$$
|\begin{aligned}a & b \\ c & d\end{aligned}|=ad-bc.
$$

Using the formula, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}(U) & =|\begin{aligned}-v & 5 \\ 4 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =-v\cdot 3-5\cdot 4 \\  & =-3v-20\end{aligned}
$$

Since $det(U)=4$, we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(U) & =4 \\ -3v-20 & =4 \\ -3v & =4+20 \\ -3v & =24 \\ v & =-8\end{aligned}
$$

q-69658.html:
Question 6
?

If U=[−v543] and det(U)=4, what is the value of v?

a
−9
b
−8
c
4
d
6
e
8
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a 2×2 matrix, the determinant is given by the formula

|abcd|=ad−bc.

Using the formula, we have:

det(U)=|−v543|=−v⋅3−5⋅4=−3v−20

Since det(U)=4, we get:

det(U)=4−3v−20=4−3v=4+20−3v=24v=−8
